title: UNIONS v2, four tomographic bins (blinded data)
summary: The four tomographic bins and n(z) of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468, measured blinded. The B-mode data vectors come first, for all ten bin pairs in three estimators, each with its errors.
banner: Blinded (blind: unions): E-mode data vectors are concealed; do not interpret cosmology
provenance: ShapePipe SP v2.0, upper bound 9 on galaxy size relative to the PSF, 20,515 of the 22,901 tiles in the v2.0.0 release; 170.6M galaxies, 4,690 deg²; tomographic footprint (tiles with z-band photometry) 16,881 tiles, 4,065 deg²
recalibrated DR6 BPZ+SOM four-bin n(z) and bins of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468, on a dz = 0.05 grid; validation and null tests only; ⟨z⟩ = 0.283, 0.451, 0.617, 0.922

figures.caption: Pure-mode B-mode correlation functions θξ₊ᴮ (circles) and θξ₋ᴮ (squares) for each pair of tomographic bins, with errors from the analytic covariance. Shaded scales lie outside the 12–83′ range of the test; the header of each panel gives the PTE of ξ₊ᴮ and of ξ₋ᴮ over that range, in red below 0.05.
figures.alt: Pure-mode B-mode correlation functions θξ₊ᴮ (circles) and θξ₋ᴮ (squares) for each pair of tomographic bins, with errors from the analytic covariance. Shaded scales lie outside the 12–83′ range of the test; the header of each panel gives the PTE of ξ₊ᴮ and of ξ₋ᴮ over that range, in red below 0.05.

figures.caption: COSEBIs B modes Bₙ (n ≤ 20, 12–83′) for each pair of tomographic bins, in units of their own standard deviation, over bands at ±1σ and ±2σ; each panel header gives the PTE over all 20 modes. The modes are correlated, so judge by the PTE rather than by single points.
figures.alt: COSEBIs B modes Bₙ (n ≤ 20, 12–83′) for each pair of tomographic bins, in units of their own standard deviation, over bands at ±1σ and ±2σ; each panel header gives the PTE over all 20 modes. The modes are correlated, so judge by the PTE rather than by single points.

figures.caption: Pseudo-Cℓ BB (filled circles) and EB (open diamonds) for each pair of tomographic bins, in units of their own standard deviation from a Gaussian NaMaster covariance, over bands at ±1σ and ±2σ. The ℓ axis is linear in √ℓ, on which the 32 bandpowers are evenly spaced; BB and EB are offset slightly in ℓ to keep them apart. Each panel header gives the PTEs over all 32 bandpowers, in red below 0.05.
figures.alt: Pseudo-Cℓ BB (filled circles) and EB (open diamonds) for each pair of tomographic bins, in units of their own standard deviation from a Gaussian NaMaster covariance, over bands at ±1σ and ±2σ. The ℓ axis is linear in √ℓ, on which the 32 bandpowers are evenly spaced; BB and EB are offset slightly in ℓ to keep them apart. Each panel header gives the PTEs over all 32 bandpowers, in red below 0.05.

figures.caption: Whole-sample ξ±ᴮ as measured (points) and after masking six objects that contaminated the PSF star sample (M33, M101, M13, M92, Draco, Ursa Minor; crosses): no point moves by more than 0.06σ. This test comes from an earlier non-tomographic run on 138M galaxies, not from this run.
figures.alt: Whole-sample ξ±ᴮ as measured (points) and after masking six objects that contaminated the PSF star sample (M33, M101, M13, M92, Draco, Ursa Minor; crosses): no point moves by more than 0.06σ. This test comes from an earlier non-tomographic run on 138M galaxies, not from this run.

figures.caption: Blinded shear correlation functions θξ₊ (filled) and θξ₋ (open) for each pair of tomographic bins, with errors from the analytic covariance. The blinding shifts these data by an unknown cosmology, so they are shown alone, without a prediction to compare against.

figures.caption: Blinded pseudo-Cℓ EE power spectra ℓCℓ for each pair of tomographic bins, on one y range and an axis linear in √ℓ, with errors from the Gaussian NaMaster covariance; shown alone for the same reason.

figures.caption: ρ statistics of the PSF stars, which measure the PSF model residuals; all four bins share them.

figures.caption: Correlations between galaxy shapes and PSF quantities for each tomographic bin (one row per bin): τ₀, and τ₂ and τ₅ multiplied by θ, with each bin's fitted leakage model as a line.
figures.alt: Correlations between galaxy shapes and PSF quantities for each tomographic bin (one row per bin): τ₀, and τ₂ and τ₅ multiplied by θ, with each bin's fitted leakage model as a line.

figures.caption: PSF-leakage coefficients α, β and η per bin, from a fit of the τ statistics to the ρ templates with ρ held fixed. The τ estimator biases α low by about 25% on a simulation with known leakage (CosmoStat/shear_psf_leakage#58), so read these α as lower limits.

figures.caption: Analytic (OneCovariance) ξ± variance divided by the data's 100-patch jackknife variance, per bin pair (auto-correlations coloured, cross-correlations grey); the band is the jackknife's own ±14% scatter. The median ratio is 1.00 below 10′ (required within 15% of 1) and 1.03 at 12–83′.
